name: Desed Synthetic Soundscapes
description: We propose a benchmark of state-of-the-art sound event detection systems (SED). We designed synthetic evaluation sets to focus on specific sound event detection challenges. We analyze the performance of the submissions to DCASE 2021 task 4 depending on time related modifications (time position of an event and length of clips) and we study the impact of non-target sound events and reverberation. We show that the localization in time of sound events is still a problem for SED systems. We also show that reverberation and non-target sound events are severely degrading the performance of the SED systems. In the latter case, sound separation seems like a promising solution.
typical_sota_score: Event-based F1 typically ≈40–70% depending on reverberation/non-target interference and evaluation condition
reputation: A specialized DCASE-related benchmark that is recognized within the sound event detection community, especially for stress-testing robustness under synthetic perturbations.
notes: Synthetic evaluation sets focus on controlled perturbations rather than broad real-world coverage; performance is highly affected by reverberation, overlap, and event timing.
